newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Toilet trouble hits Mir space crew.
newsitem.headline: Toilet trouble hits Mir space crew.

text.p: The three-man Russian-American crew of the Mir space station is in trouble -- toilet trouble.
Containers holding their bodily waste fluids are filling up fast and replacements, held up by cash problems in Russia, are not due for weeks, Interfax news agency said on Wednesday.
Space agency officials could not be reached for comment.
Quoting unidentified sources, Interfax said a device which recycles the crew's waste into the craft's cooling system had broken down and all the reserve containers were nearly full.
The crew could also not find the pump used to transfer the waste water into the cooling system, it added.
New waste containers were due to be shipped out in October but financial problems meant the supply ship was not able to leave. It will not be launched until November 20.
U.S. astronaut John Blaha and his two Russian colleagues, Valery Korzun and Alexander Koleri, have been on the ageing 10-year-old Mir station since September 19.
The supply ship was the fourth to be delayed this year.
